snapshot.text: Finnair, the Finnish network carrier, ended FY2024 with revenue up {{revenue.change@FY2024}} to {{revenue@FY2024}} but a weaker earnings base, as industrial action in Finland led to flight cancellations in the early and late parts of the year.
The EBITDA margin fell by {{ebitda_margin.change@FY2024}} to {{ebitda_margin@FY2024}}, and net leverage rose by {{net_leverage.change@FY2024}} to {{net_leverage@FY2024}}.

The point to watch is leverage against the network peers: net leverage of {{net_leverage@FY2024}} is above the peer median of {{net_leverage.peer_median@FY2024}} and ranks {{net_leverage.peer_rank@FY2024}}.

credit_metrics.text: EBITDA fell by {{ebitda.change@FY2024}} to {{ebitda@FY2024}}, and operating profit declined by {{operating_profit.change@FY2024}} to {{operating_profit@FY2024}}.

Total debt was reduced by {{total_debt.change@FY2024}} to {{total_debt@FY2024}} and net debt by {{net_debt.change@FY2024}} to {{net_debt@FY2024}}, but the smaller earnings base pushed gross leverage up by {{gross_leverage.change@FY2024}} to {{gross_leverage@FY2024}}.

Interest coverage improved by {{interest_coverage.change@FY2024}} to {{interest_coverage@FY2024}}, while FFO fell by {{ffo.change@FY2024}} to {{ffo@FY2024}} and FFO to debt was broadly unchanged at {{ffo_to_debt@FY2024}}.

Free cash flow rose by {{fcf.change@FY2024}} to {{fcf@FY2024}}, lifting FCF to debt by {{fcf_to_debt.change@FY2024}} to {{fcf_to_debt@FY2024}}, helped by capex intensity easing by {{capex_intensity.change@FY2024}} to {{capex_intensity@FY2024}}.

operating_performance.text: Passengers rose by {{passengers.change@FY2024}} to {{passengers@FY2024}}, while revenue grew by {{revenue.change@FY2024}} to {{revenue@FY2024}}.
The fuel share of costs fell by {{fuel_share_of_costs.change@FY2024}} to {{fuel_share_of_costs@FY2024}}, still above the peer median of {{fuel_share_of_costs.peer_median@FY2024}}.
The fleet was broadly unchanged at {{fleet@FY2024}} aircraft, with a new A350 delivered and a leased A350 and a leased A321 purchased during the year.

liquidity_funding.text: Cash and cash-like investments fell by {{cash_like.change@FY2024}} to {{cash_like@FY2024}}, and cash liquidity to revenue declined by {{cash_liquidity_to_revenue.change@FY2024}} to {{cash_liquidity_to_revenue@FY2024}}.
Total liquidity of {{liquidity@FY2024}} included {{undrawn_facilities@FY2024}} of undrawn committed facilities, and liquidity to revenue reached {{liquidity_to_revenue@FY2024}}.

Advance ticket cover rose by {{advance_ticket_cover.change@FY2024}} to {{advance_ticket_cover@FY2024}}, with contract liabilities up {{contract_liabilities.change@FY2024}} to {{contract_liabilities@FY2024}}, so a larger share of liquidity is customer prepayments.
Funding was refinanced during the year, with a new unsecured senior bond issued to replace the old one and a new secured revolving credit facility agreed for general corporate purposes.

peer_positioning.text: Finnair sits in the middle of the network group on EBITDA margin ({{ebitda_margin.peer_rank@FY2024}}), FCF to debt ({{fcf_to_debt.peer_rank@FY2024}}) and cash liquidity to revenue ({{cash_liquidity_to_revenue.peer_rank@FY2024}}).

Leverage is the weakest in the group: gross leverage ranks {{gross_leverage.peer_rank@FY2024}} against a peer median of {{gross_leverage.peer_median@FY2024}}, and net leverage ranks {{net_leverage.peer_rank@FY2024}}.

Coverage and cash generation also trail the group, with interest coverage ranking {{interest_coverage.peer_rank@FY2024}} against a peer median of {{interest_coverage.peer_median@FY2024}} and FFO to debt ranking {{ffo_to_debt.peer_rank@FY2024}} against {{ffo_to_debt.peer_median@FY2024}}.

Capex intensity of {{capex_intensity@FY2024}} is below the peer median of {{capex_intensity.peer_median@FY2024}}, and advance ticket cover sits in the middle of the group ({{advance_ticket_cover.peer_rank@FY2024}}).

watch_items.text: Leverage: net leverage rose by {{net_leverage.change@FY2024}} to {{net_leverage@FY2024}} as EBITDA fell by {{ebitda.change@FY2024}}, the weakest net leverage in the network group ({{net_leverage.peer_rank@FY2024}}).

Cash generation: FFO to debt of {{ffo_to_debt@FY2024}} is below the peer median of {{ffo_to_debt.peer_median@FY2024}} and ranks {{ffo_to_debt.peer_rank@FY2024}}, so the improvement in FCF to debt rests on lower capital spending.

Liquidity: cash liquidity to revenue fell by {{cash_liquidity_to_revenue.change@FY2024}} to {{cash_liquidity_to_revenue@FY2024}}, with cash and cash-like investments down {{cash_like.change@FY2024}} to {{cash_like@FY2024}}.

Customer prepayments: advance ticket cover rose by {{advance_ticket_cover.change@FY2024}} to {{advance_ticket_cover@FY2024}}, in line with the peer median, so a larger part of liquidity is refundable if bookings slow.
